organization: The New York Academy of Sciences (NYAS)
secondary_character: mentored STEM innovation challenges using research methods — NOT original publishable research; see honest_scope below
self_registration_note: Student applies directly. No school nomination, no national body. Combined with zero cost and global eligibility, this is the lowest-barrier genuine STEM opportunity found in this lane.
age_note: Fits ORYN's stated 14-18 band almost exactly, and uniquely reaches DOWN to 13 — most flagship opportunities are effectively 16+.
eligibility_verbatim: 'Students and mentors can participate from anywhere in the world'; the programme operates 'across 100+ countries'.
eligibility_placement: Stated in the programme's own eligibility description, not a marketing banner. Meets the placement test.
cost_verbatim: 'The Junior Academy is completely free for participating students'; 'No purchase or payment of any kind is necessary'
what_students_do_verbatim: Students 'form international teams and work with STEM experts' on 'Innovation Challenges where they collaborate under the guidance of STEM mentors to design solutions to real-world problems.' Challenges involve 'research methods, design thinking and data analysis.'
honest_scope: CLASSIFY PRECISELY: this is mentored team innovation work that USES research methods — it is not an original-research programme producing a paper, the way RSI, Pioneer or a TÜBİTAK 2204-A project is. It genuinely strengthens a research-adjacent profile and it is real, structured, mentored work; it should not be sold to a student as equivalent to conducting original research. Recording it as plain 'research' without this distinction is how the corpus got into trouble in the first place.
cycle_evidence: 'Applications close: July 2, 2026' for the Fall 2026 cohort — already past at retrieval (2026-08-23).
deadline_note: Next cohort's date not published. NYAS has historically run more than one intake per year; do NOT infer a schedule.
selectivity: 'Each year, we receive thousands of applications' and 'we take the application process very seriously'. No acceptance rate published.
why_high_value: Free + worldwide + direct student application + ages 13-17 is a combination almost nothing else in this lane offers. For an international student with no national-olympiad route and no money, this is one of very few real doors. Absent from the corpus.
unresolved: Next intake date.
Time commitment per challenge.
Whether mentors are guaranteed or matched competitively.

organization: British Science Association (supported by UK Research and Innovation and Urenco)
self_registration_note: Projects are submitted and administered through a school/centre and assessed by a CREST assessor; the site does not describe an individual-student route.
age_note: 'Typical' — the award levels are described as typical ages, not hard limits. Do not store as a hard minimum_age.
effort_verbatim: 'Typically 70 hrs to complete'; Gold is described as 'A high-level, open-ended, independently led STEM investigation requiring around 70 hours of work demonstrating originality and depth.'
effort_note: ~70 hours is a genuine, quantified time cost — unusually explicit, and directly usable by ORYN's time-budget logic (spec §64). Most opportunity records carry no effort estimate at all.
cost_note: TWO PRICES, and the column can hold only one. £30 UK / £40 International. Whichever is stored will be wrong for half of ORYN's users, and the column carries no currency either — a stored '30' reads as dollars to any model that never sees the unit.
assessment_verbatim: 'Upload the Gold project work alongside a profile form of each student.' A 'CREST assessor' evaluates each Gold project; students 'must meet at least 11 of 15 criteria' to earn the award.
international_eligibility: IMPLIED BUT NOT STATED. The published international price strongly implies non-UK participation is possible, but no sentence on the pages retrieved says so. Per the placement rule, a price list is not an eligibility statement — recorded as unconfirmed.
deadline_note: NOT STATED. The pages give no deadline and no statement that entry is continuous. Deliberately NOT recorded as rolling — absence of a deadline is not evidence of rolling intake.
scotland_note: The site announces free access in Scotland; terms not retrieved.
why_notable: One of the few structured, assessed, low-cost routes to a recognised independent-research credential, with a published hour cost. Good fit for a student who wants research depth without a competitive selection gate.
unresolved: Explicit statement that non-UK students may participate.
Whether an individual student can register without a school.
Whether entry is genuinely continuous.
Scotland free-access terms.

self_registration_note: Framed around schools: 'introduce real research in your own school using one of our free research projects.' No individual-student route stated.
mission_verbatim: IRIS aims to 'change the culture of UK education so that every young person can take part in authentic research and innovation while at school.'
research_nature: GENUINE ORIGINAL RESEARCH. Named live projects include Big Data: ATLAS (CERN data), DNA Origami, Cosmic Mining, Earth Observation, Carbon Researchers, Elephants on the Move, Future Flight, Greener Fragrances, Wild Things, and an 'Original Research' strand.
research_nature_note: Students analyse real datasets from real collaborations — this is closer to RSI/BL4S in substance than to a taught course, and it is free.
eligible_countries: UK — inferred from framing, NOT from an explicit rule
eligibility_caution: The site repeatedly says 'UK education' but I found no sentence stating that non-UK schools are excluded. Recorded as UK-oriented, NOT as UK-restricted. Do not tell a non-UK student they are barred without checking.
unresolved: Age/year-group eligibility.
Whether a student outside the UK, or a student whose school is not a member, can take part at all.
How and when a school joins.
deadline_note: NOT STATED. The site gives no deadline and no statement that entry is continuous — deliberately not recorded as rolling.

organization: MIT PRIMES and Art of Problem Solving (AoPS), jointly
secondary_character: genuine original mathematical research producing peer-reviewed publications with student co-authors
self_registration_note: NO SELECTION GATE AT ALL. No application, no nomination, no national body, no fee. A student joins the open project and contributes. Across everything researched in this lane, this is the only genuine-research opportunity with zero admission barrier.
eligibility_verbatim: 'CrowdMath is an open project that gives all high school and college students the opportunity to collaborate on a large research project with top-tier research mentors and an exceptional peer group.' MIT PRIMES' own page describes CrowdMath as 'open to all high school and college students around the world'.
eligibility_placement: Stated in the project's own description of who it is for, on both the AoPS project page and the MIT PRIMES programme page. Two independent official sources, both in the eligibility position. Meets the placement test.
cost_note: No fee stated anywhere; an AoPS account is required to participate. Recorded as free, but note the free-ness is by absence-of-fee plus the 'open project' framing rather than an explicit 'this is free' sentence.
what_students_do: Collaborate publicly on an open research problem with mentors, over a year-long project. Current project: 'MIT PRIMES 2026: Arithmetic Conjectures on Rational Semirings'. Fourteen projects run since 2016.
output_evidence: THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. CrowdMath output is real published mathematics with named student co-authors, e.g. 'On the Atomicity of Power Monoids of Puiseux Monoids' (CrowdMath-2023) published in International Journal of Algebra and Computation 35:02 (2025) 167-181; 'Factorization in Additive Monoids of Evaluation Polynomial Semirings' (CrowdMath-2022) published in Communications in Algebra 51:10 (2023) 4347-4362; 'Sequence saturation' (CrowdMath-2021) published in Discrete Applied Mathematics 360 (2025) 382-393; 'Extremal results for graphs of bounded metric dimension' (CrowdMath-2020) in Discrete Applied Mathematics 309 (2022); plus arXiv preprints from 2016 onward. Most recent listed: 24 July 2026.
output_note: Compare this to the paid student journals in the corpus. A student pays JRHS $350 at submission for a ~30% shot at a high-school journal; CrowdMath costs nothing and its participants appear as co-authors in actual peer-reviewed mathematics journals. That contrast is, on its own, a strong answer to ORYN's central question of where a student's time and money are best spent.
cycle_note: A project is live (MIT PRIMES 2026). Projects run annually; new ones open each year. No deadline stated — and I am NOT recording this as rolling: it is an open collaborative project, which is a different shape from a rolling intake.
fetch_method: Browser pane (WebFetch received HTTP 403 from artofproblemsolving.com)
why_high_value: ORYN's research gap is worst for students with no money, no mentor and no national route — precisely the students the rest of this corpus cannot serve. CrowdMath is free, worldwide, ungated, mentored, and demonstrably produces published research. It is the strongest single answer found tonight to 'how does this student start doing real research?', and it is absent from the corpus.
honest_caveats: Pure mathematics only, and hard: the problems are genuine open research at a level far above olympiad training. Contribution is self-directed with no guarantee of authorship — co-authorship depends on making a real contribution. This should be recommended as a high-ceiling, high-effort option for a mathematically strong student, not as an easy win.
unresolved: Whether any structured onboarding or minimum background is stated for new participants.
How co-authorship is decided.
deadline_note: No deadline by design: CrowdMath is an open collaborative project a student joins, not an intake with a closing date. Explicitly NOT rolling — a different shape from a rolling intake.

canonical_name: Research Placements and Experiences (formerly Nuffield Research Placements)
organization: STEM Learning Ltd (National STEM Learning Centre, University of York); funded by partners
name_change_note: IMPORTANT FOR DEDUPE AND SEARCH: nuffieldresearchplacements.org now 301-redirects to stem.org.uk/placements. Anyone searching the corpus for 'Nuffield Research Placements' must land here. If a Nuffield-named row exists anywhere, it is the same programme under an old name.
eligibility_all_required: 'Be over 16 years old and in Year 12 or S5.'
'Be in full-time, state-funded education in the UK.'
'Have at least 5 GCSEs at Level 5 or above OR Scottish Nationals at Level B or above, including maths, a science subject and English (or another humanities subject).'
'Be studying one or more A-levels or Scottish Highers (or equivalent) in science, technology, engineering, economics, geography, psychology, computing, statistics or maths.'
'Be available for 1-2 consecutive weeks over July and/or August to collaborate with your Placement Provider.'
eligibility_at_least_one_required: 'Be living, or have lived, in local authority care.'
'Come from a family with a combined household income of below £40,000 a year (pre-tax).'
'Be entitled to free school meals, either now or at any time in the last six years.'
'In receipt of, or entitled to, discretionary payments at school/college (e.g., EMA, 16-19 Bursary Fund).'
'Be the first in your immediate family to participate in higher education (not including any older siblings).'
eligibility_note: DECISION-CRITICAL AND HIGHLY RESTRICTIVE. This is a widening-participation programme: a student must satisfy EVERY criterion in the first list AND AT LEAST ONE in the second. Two consequences an advisor must get right: (a) 'full-time, state-funded education in the UK' excludes independent fee-paying school students — the site has a dedicated FAQ on exactly this; (b) it is UK-only and year-group-locked to Year 12 / S5. Recommending this to a student who does not meet the second list wastes their time, and the programme's own page states '100% of students taking part are from low-income backgrounds, under-represented groups or are the first in their family to attend university.'
cost_verbatim: 'You can take part in a placement at no cost. You will receive a subsidy to cover expenses such as travel.'
what_students_do_verbatim: 'Research Placements are 2-week collaborations with a STEM-related knowledge expert on a live research question or area of development. While producing a scientific or technical report and poster, this opportunity ensures that students contribute meaningfully to the host organisation's current work.'
research_nature: GENUINE. Output is a scientific/technical report and poster from work on a live research question. FAQ: projects range from lab and fieldwork to 'ambitious social science projects (using data science to investigate big political and social issues)' — 'Not all science is done in the lab.'
two_variants: Research Placements (2 weeks, report + poster) vs Experience Placements (5 days, workbook + reflective report). Only the former is genuine research; the latter is career exploration. They must NOT be conflated in one record.
cycle_timetable_verbatim: 'WINTER — Applications open in December. Check your eligibility and apply. SPRING — Applications close and successful applicants choose placements. SUMMER — Begin work on your pre-placement independent study assignments and attend an induction event. AUTUMN — Submit your final report, poster and feedback form.'
cycle_timetable_note: An official, published annual rhythm: opens in December. That is genuinely actionable forward guidance — a Year 11 student can plan for it — without inventing a specific date.
progression_note: The programme's own page states a placement can 'Lead to applications for a Gold CREST Award or the Big Bang Competition' — a real, officially-stated pathway linking this to CR1-051 (CREST Gold). Worth modelling as a sequence rather than as unrelated rows.
selectivity: Meeting the criteria does not guarantee a placement — the site carries a dedicated FAQ 'If I meet the eligibility criteria am I guaranteed a placement?'. No ratio published.
fetch_method: Browser pane (WebFetch received HTTP 403 / Cloudflare challenge on stem.org.uk)
unresolved: Exact December opening date for the next cycle.
Whether any non-UK student can ever qualify — the criteria as written say no.

organization: NOT STATED on the page retrieved
secondary_character: genuine research — every participant presents their own research report
identity_caution: THREE DIFFERENT ENTITIES SHARE THIS ACRONYM. (a) THIS one — the secondary-school research conference at icysconference.com; (b) the International Center for Young Scientists at NIMS Japan (nims.go.jp/icys), a POSTDOCTORAL research centre, not a student competition; (c) the International Conference of Young Social Scientists (icysss.edu.rs), a separate event. age_rule_verbatim: 'a special type of individual competition...for 14-18 year-old secondary school students'

what_students_do_verbatim: 'Every participant has to prepare a research report on a subject chosen by herself/himself', delivered as 'ten-minute reports' evaluated by 'an international jury'.
what_students_do_note: Subject is chosen BY THE STUDENT, and the format is a short spoken presentation in English rather than a written paper — a materially different demand from ISEF/TÜBİTAK, and a good fit for a student whose strength is communication.
entry_mechanism: NOT STATED on the page retrieved. ICYS has historically operated through national delegations; that is NOT confirmed here and must not be asserted.
cycle_evidence: Host listed as Thailand; the year visible in the organisers list is 2025. No 2026 or 2027 edition confirmed on the page retrieved.
classification_reason: Held at B: the nature, age band and format are P1-solid and genuinely valuable, but entry mechanism, country eligibility, cost and current cycle are all unknown. Not fit to recommend to a specific student yet.

canonical_name: MIT PRIMES (Program for Research in Mathematics, Engineering and Science for High School Students)

sub_programmes.name: MIT PRIMES
sub_programmes.eligibility: 'high school juniors and sophomores' 'from Greater Boston'

sub_programmes.name: PRIMES-USA
sub_programmes.eligibility: 'high school juniors and sophomores' 'from across the United States (outside of Greater Boston)'

sub_programmes.name: CrowdMath
sub_programmes.eligibility: 'open to all high school and college students around the world' — see CR1-053

sub_programme_note: PRIMES is an umbrella of six distinct programmes with DIFFERENT eligibility. A single corpus row titled 'MIT PRIMES' would be wrong for five of them. Yulia's Dream in particular is restricted to students from Ukraine — an eligibility rule that would be invisible under an umbrella record.
residency_rule_verbatim: PRIMES is 'available only to students who reside in the United States'.
international_route_verbatim: 'International students are welcome to participate in CrowdMath'
international_route_note: HIGH-VALUE: MIT itself states the alternative route. An international student asking about PRIMES should be told, on the operator's own authority, that PRIMES is closed to them and CrowdMath (CR1-053) is the open door — free, worldwide, same MIT mentors. This is the 'find the open door instead of reporting the closed one' pattern, and here it is officially sanctioned rather than inferred.
deadline_note: NOT STATED on the pages retrieved. PRIMES has historically closed applications around the turn of the year; do NOT record an inferred date.
unresolved: Application deadline for the next cycle.

organization: Stony Brook University, Office of Academic Engagement
what_students_do_verbatim: 'engage in hands-on research in science, math or engineering' — students 'work with distinguished faculty mentors, learn laboratory techniques and tools, become part of active research teams, and experience life at a research university'
cycle_verbatim: 'Applications for SimonsSRP 2026 are closed. No late applications will be considered'
deadline_note: 'Due to the large volume of applications received for this program, late submissions/materials are not considered/accepted.' Exact date not located on this page this pass -- the accordion for 'Important Dates' was not successfully opened before this record was finalized.
eligibility: 'academically talented, motivated high school students' — grade, age, citizenship and residency ALL NOT STATED on the page retrieved
cost_note: Still not stated on any page retrieved. A 'Stipends' link exists on the main site but was not opened this pass.
classification_reason: UPGRADED from C_INCOMPLETE. The eligibility content on stonybrook.edu is behind an accordion widget that a page-text extraction does not expand by default -- clicking it revealed the full rule. Same lesson as tonight's other rendering-layer cases (Google Sites CSV/Doc export, IPhO/IChO Statutes): the fact was one interaction away, not genuinely undocumented.
unresolved: Exact application deadline date (program dates known: 29 June - 7 August 2026; the 'Important Dates' accordion was not opened this pass).
Stipend amount, if any.
eligibility_verbatim: 'Applicants must currently be in their junior year (11th grade) of high school at the time of applying; must be US citizens and/or permanent residents; and must be at least 16 years of age by the start of the program. (No exceptions.)'
grade_rule: 11th grade (junior year) ONLY -- explicitly not open to 10th or 12th graders.
citizenship_rule_verbatim: must be US citizens and/or permanent residents
no_exceptions_verbatim: '(No exceptions.)' -- stated in the eligibility rule itself, immediately after the age clause.
nomination_requirement_verbatim: 'Interested eligible applicants should seek nomination from their high school... We recommend that only one official at each school... be responsible for nominating students to ensure there are no more than 2 nominees per school (more than 2 nominees will result in the disqualification of all applicants).'
nomination_note: A hard institutional gate: max 2 nominees per school, and exceeding it disqualifies ALL of that school's applicants -- not just the excess ones. A student cannot simply decide to apply; their school must actively nominate them, and coordinate to stay under the cap.
selectivity_verbatim: 'Percentage of students admitted: about <5%'; 'admissions into the Simons program is highly selective and we receive far more applications from qualified students than we can accommodate.'
confidence_note: High on eligibility, nomination gate, and selectivity -- all now sourced directly. Cost and the exact application deadline date remain the honest gaps.

eligibility_caution: The clause listing state-funded / home-educated / community-group entrants may or may not EXCLUDE independent-school students — the page as retrieved reads as a description of who is covered rather than an explicit exclusion. NOT resolved. Do not tell an independent-school student either way.
cost_verbatim: 'The Big Bang UK Young Scientists & Engineers Competition is free'
team_rule_verbatim: 'Competitors can only enter one project, either on their own or as part of a team.'
deadline_note: NOT STATED on the page retrieved.
progression_link: Named by STEM Learning (CR1-054) as a destination a Research Placement can lead to, alongside Gold CREST. The UK therefore has a coherent officially-stated ladder: Research Placement -> Gold CREST / Big Bang.

secondary_character: awarded for a completed significant piece of work, including original research — functions as a research prize, not a needs-based scholarship
self_registration_note: Student applies directly, but must supply 'two nominator forms' — so two adults are required even though no institution gates entry.
age_rule_verbatim: 'Applicants must be 18 or younger as of the application deadline'
citizenship_rule_verbatim: 'Be a U.S. citizen residing in the United States, or a Permanent Resident of the United States residing in the United States, or be stationed overseas due to active U.S. military duty.'
citizenship_note: STRICT AND DOUBLE-BARRELLED: citizenship/PR status AND residence in the US are both required — unlike Regeneron STS, where living and studying in the US is enough regardless of citizenship. The two US flagships resolve the same student's case oppositely, so the rules must not be generalised across them.
award_note: The largest single award found anywhere in this lane.
categories_verbatim: 'Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Literature, Music, Philosophy and Outside the Box'
categories_note: Notably NOT STEM-only. Literature, Music, Philosophy and an explicit 'Outside the Box' category mean a humanities or arts student with a serious body of work has a real route here — rare among high-value awards and directly useful for ORYN students whose strength is not science.
submission_verbatim: Students must submit 'a significant piece of work' plus 'two nominator forms and all of the Attachments.'
cycle_verbatim: 'The 2026 application is closed. The 2027 application will open in the Fall of 2026.'
cycle_note: Opens in Fall 2026 — i.e. within weeks of retrieval. Genuinely near-term and worth surfacing now to any eligible student, even though no exact date is published.
unresolved: Exact opening and closing dates for the 2027 cycle.
What counts as a 'significant piece of work' per category.
Who may serve as a nominator.
deadline_note: No date published yet. The official page states only 'The 2026 application is closed. The 2027 application will open in the Fall of 2026.' Opening is imminent relative to retrieval; the exact date must be re-checked, not inferred.
